paras_en: U.S. equity indices opened relatively unchanged on Wednesday (the 2nd), as oil prices fell from recent highs, slightly easing market concerns that rising energy costs could fuel inflation, but Treasury yields remain at multi‑year highs, continuing to dampen investors' risk appetite.

West Texas Intermediate crude slipped below $90 a barrel, halting a two‑day rally sparked by the U.S.–Iran contest over control of the Hormuz Strait; the U.S. 10‑year Treasury yield steadied after reaching a two‑year peak.

At the time of writing, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up about 260 points, or roughly 0.5%, the Nasdaq Composite down about 20 points, or 0.07%, the S&P 500 up about 0.1%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down about 0.1%. TSMC ADR rose about 0.3%.

International oil prices paused their recent gains, modestly easing worries that energy costs could push inflation higher, and U.S. stock futures narrowed their declines in pre‑market trading on Wednesday, while Treasury prices rose in tandem. However, global sovereign‑bond yields still face upward pressure, and with major central banks likely to hike rates this month, market sentiment remains cautious.

At the time of writing, S&P 500 futures were roughly flat. Dell Technologies (DELL‑US) rose in pre‑market trading after a strong revenue outlook, the European Stoxx 600 fell 0.3%, Asian markets posted their biggest drop in two weeks, and the dollar was little changed.

Brent crude fell back to around $94 a barrel after two days of gains. U.S. Treasuries moved higher despite the dip, with the 30‑year yield down two basis points to 5.25%, while most other bond markets kept falling. ADP data released on Wednesday showed U.S. private‑sector employment added 38,000 jobs in August, below expectations and indicating a slowdown in hiring momentum.

The oil price pullback temporarily eases market pressure. Previously, sustained energy‑price gains had deepened investors' fears of a renewed inflation surge and further weakened a bond market already strained by massive government borrowing and corporate financing needs.

Traders now estimate that the probability of a rate hike this month exceeds 50% at three major central banks, including the Fed, with the Fed's odds around 65%. ING strategist Chris Turner said the market’s new baseline appears to be a Fed hike in September. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has made clear that inflation is still falling too slowly to hit target, and with the economy showing resilience, the Fed may have to act.

Although global bond markets are under selling pressure, yield increases have been relatively modest, offering some comfort to traders. BNP Paribas wealth‑management strategist Stephan Kemper said the current bond‑market decline is orderly and broad‑based, not driven by credit risk or liquidity strain, suggesting markets are pricing in a longer‑term high‑rate environment rather than a credit crisis or recession.

Kemper added that whether yields retreat will hinge on inflation expectations. If long‑term yield pressure eases and corporate fundamentals stay strong, equities could rally sharply. Corporate cash balances have rebounded to historic highs amid a surge in AI spending, supporting stocks. So far this year, global equities have attracted about $1.1 trillion of inflows, the largest since 2021.

Nevertheless, Global Gate Asset Management strategist Patrik Lang warned that if U.S. and Japanese sovereign‑bond yields break through current resistance zones, equity resilience could be tested. Investor positioning is elevated and short‑term indicators have entered overbought territory, meaning markets may enter a consolidation phase over the next few weeks regardless of fundamentals.

paras_en: September 2, 2026 (U‑Analysis/Industry Data Center) — U.S. corporate insiders have been buying more of their own companies' stock recently. According to filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the most notable increase involves Republic Services (RSG‑US), the leading waste‑management and environmental services company.

Republic Services primarily handles garbage collection, recycling, transfer and landfill operations, and provides hazardous and industrial waste treatment services, ranking alongside Waste Management (WM‑US) as the two biggest players in the U.S. waste‑management sector. Cascade Investment purchased a total of 560,100 shares of Republic Services on August 26‑27 at an average price of about $220.52 per share, amounting to roughly $124 million.

items.title: Cerebras芬蘭擴建AI資料中心｜簽下165MW長約首期50MW已動工
items.title_en: Cerebras Expands AI Data Center in Finland, Signs 165MW Contract with First 50MW Under Construction
paras: 2026年09月02日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ AI晶片業者Cerebras Systems(CBRS-US)宣布與Compute Nordic Finland合作，在芬蘭Mikkeli興建大型AI資料中心，規劃IT容量最高達165MW，首期50MW已開始施工，後續將分階段擴至80MW及165MW。
值得注意的是，這項計畫並非單純先蓋再找需求。雙方已透過一系列服務訂單簽訂7年期合約，代表部分AI算力需求已轉化為長期承諾，也讓Cerebras取得支撐全球AI運算服務擴張所需的資料中心容量。
隨AI資料中心功率密度持續提高，電力與冷卻已成為擴張關鍵。Mikkeli資料中心將採用封閉循環冷卻系統，降低持續取用市政用水的需求，並規劃回收AI運算產生的廢熱。Cerebras表示，目標是在每MW電力下提高可產出的有效AI算力。
根據Ramboll研究估算，若最終擴建至165MW，整體投資規模約10~17億歐元。

paras_en: On September 2, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center report) – AI chip maker Cerebras Systems (CBRS-US) announced a partnership with Compute Nordic Finland to build a large AI data center in Mikkeli, Finland, planning a maximum IT capacity of 165 MW, with the first phase of 50 MW already under construction and later phases to expand to 80 MW and ultimately 165 MW.

It is noteworthy that this project is not simply built first and then find demand. The two parties have already signed a series of service orders covering a seven‑year contract, meaning that part of the AI compute demand has been converted into a long‑term commitment, giving Cerebras the data‑center capacity needed to support the expansion of its global AI computing services.

As AI data‑center power density continues to rise, power and cooling become critical to expansion. The Mikkeli data center will use a closed‑loop cooling system to reduce continuous municipal water usage and will plan to recycle waste heat generated by AI computing. Cerebras says its goal is to increase the effective AI compute output per megawatt of power.
According to a Ramboll study, if the expansion reaches the full 165 MW, the total investment is estimated at roughly €1.0‑1.7 billion.

items.title_en: Why Berkshire Is Buying Alphabet in a Frenzy? Abel Reveals the Key Reason
paras: 波克夏海瑟威(BRK.A-US)(BRK.B-US)執行長阿貝爾(Greg Abel)周三(2日)表示，Google母公司Alphabet(GOOGL-US)(GOOG-US)是人工智慧(AI)領域的「重要參與者」。波克夏第二季大舉加碼Alphabet，使其一躍成為公司股票投資組合的第三大持股。
阿貝爾接受《CNBC》訪問時表示，波克夏可從旗下企業實際運用AI的情況，清楚掌握這項技術帶來的影響及效益，因而進一步提高投資興趣，同時看好Google在AI競賽中的強勢地位。
阿貝爾透露，波克夏15個月前以折價6.5%的條件，取得價值100億美元的Google持股。當時交易規模尚未確定，但對方建議波克夏考慮投入100億美元，阿貝爾隨後與巴菲特(Warren Buffett)討論投資金額及折價幅度，最終完成交易。
根據波克夏8月向美國證券交易委員會(SEC)提交的第二季持股資料，公司當季增持總值約170億美元的Alphabet股票，成為該季最大規模的新增投資。截至最新申報，波克夏持有約1.06億股Alphabet A類與C類股票，按目前市價計算，價值約366億美元。
除Alphabet外，波克夏第二季也大舉加碼達美航空(DAL-US)，持股規模增加44%，增持價值約16億美元。不過Alphabet在波克夏投資組合中的地位明顯提升，凸顯阿貝爾與巴菲特對其AI發展潛力的信心。
Google與微軟(MSFT-US)、Meta(META-US)、亞馬遜(AMZN-US)及甲骨文(ORCL-US)並列五大超大規模雲端服務業者，正投入鉅額資本支出，擴充運行AI所需的資料中心與運算能力。
高盛(GS-US)估計，2026年全球超大規模雲端業者資本支出可能接近1兆美元，但各機構預測差異相當大。高盛研究人員指出，市場普遍引用的7,940億美元預測，可能低估全球AI資本支出約2,000億美元，卻也可能高估美國境內AI投資相同金額。
對投資人而言，關鍵仍是這些龐大支出何時能轉化為回報。高盛警告，若AI運算需求持續由模型訓練主導，企業在廣泛商業化之前仍須不斷投入資本支出與研發經費，投資報酬實現的時間可能進一步延後。
paras_en: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A-US)(BRK.B-US) CEO Greg Abel told CNBC on Wednesday (Feb. 2) that Alphabet (GOOGL-US)(GOOG-US), Google’s parent company, is a "key player" in the AI arena. Berkshire’s second‑quarter investment in Alphabet surged, making it the company’s third‑largest holding in its equity portfolio.

Abel said Berkshire can clearly see the impact and benefits of AI through its subsidiaries’ actual use of the technology, which has further increased its investment interest and confidence in Google’s strong position in the AI race.

Abel revealed that Berkshire acquired $10 billion of Google shares 15 months ago at a 6.5% discount. At the time the transaction size was not yet determined, but the counterparty suggested Berkshire consider investing $10 billion. Abel then discussed the investment amount and discount with Warren Buffett, and the deal was ultimately completed.

According to Berkshire’s second‑quarter holdings filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in August, the company increased its Alphabet stake by about $17 billion, the largest new investment of the quarter. As of the latest filing, Berkshire holds roughly 106 million shares of Alphabet Class A and C, valued at about $36.6 billion at current prices.

In addition to Alphabet, Berkshire also significantly increased its stake in Delta Air Lines (DAL-US) in the second quarter, raising its holdings by 44% and adding about $1.6 billion. However, Alphabet’s prominence in Berkshire’s portfolio has clearly risen, underscoring Abel’s and Buffett’s confidence in its AI growth potential.

Google, Microsoft (MSFT-US), Meta (META-US), Amazon (AMZN-US) and Oracle (ORCL-US) are the five largest hyperscale cloud providers, all investing heavily in capital expenditures to expand the data centers and computing power needed to run AI.

Goldman Sachs (GS-US) estimates that global hyperscale cloud spend could approach $1 trillion in 2026, but forecasts vary widely. Goldman research notes that the commonly cited $794 billion figure may underestimate global AI capital spend by about $200 billion, while possibly overestimating U.S.‑based AI investment by the same amount.

For investors, the key question remains when these massive expenditures will translate into returns. Goldman warns that if AI compute demand continues to be dominated by model training, companies will need to keep investing in capital and R&D before widespread commercialization, potentially delaying the realization of investment returns.

paras: 日元周三(2日)盤中突然快速升值，在20國集團(G20)會議即將落幕之際，引發日本與美國可能再次進場干預匯市的揣測。由於當時沒有明顯新聞或總體經濟因素足以解釋這波走勢，市場交易室隨即傳出官方出手買進日元的說法。
日元稍早一度貶破160日元兌1美元，隨後突然急速反彈，但漲勢並未持續擴大。市場人士認為，160日元可能已成為美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)與日本銀行(BOJ)共同防守的新底線。
美國銀行(BAC-US)外匯策略師Alex Cohen表示，市場仍對匯市干預保持高度警戒。部分交易員則認為，這波升勢可能只是市場掃除停損單，也就是日元貶破關鍵價位後，引發大量部位自動平倉；不過，仍不能排除相關走勢是由官方力量觸發。
Monex外匯交易員Andrew Hazlett表示，市場確實傳出官方干預的消息，但就本次波動幅度而言，他對這項說法持懷疑態度。然而，日元兌美元與歐元同時突然走強，也很難以其他原因解釋。
這次日元升幅仍小於約一個月前的行情。當時日元一度貶至約164日元兌1美元，創近40年低點，隨後東京與華府聯手進場支撐日元，推動日元反彈約5%。
那是美日自1998年以來首次協調買進日元，也是數十年來罕見的聯合匯市干預。兩國政府事後均暗示，如有必要不排除再次採取共同行動，大幅提高做空日元的風險。隨著160日元關卡再度失守，交易員正密切觀察官方是否已悄然出手，或準備進行新一輪干預。
paras_en: The yen suddenly surged mid‑session on Wednesday (the 2nd), just as the G20 summit was winding down, prompting speculation that Japan and the United States might intervene in the currency market again. Because there was no obvious news or macro‑economic factor to explain the move, market desks quickly began circulating rumors that officials were buying yen.

Earlier the yen had slipped past the ¥160 per US$1 mark, then abruptly rebounded, though the rally did not continue to expand. Market participants think the ¥160 level may have become a new defensive floor jointly defended by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and the Bank of Japan.

Bank of America (BAC-US) FX strategist Alex Cohen said the market remains on high alert for currency‑market intervention. Some traders believe the rise may simply be a market‑wide stop‑loss sweep—positions automatically liquidated after the yen broke a key level—but they do not rule out that the move was triggered by official forces.

Monex FX trader Andrew Hazlett noted that rumors of official intervention are indeed circulating, but given the modest size of this move he is skeptical of that claim. Still, the simultaneous strength of the yen against both the dollar and the euro is hard to explain by any other reason.

The current yen gain is smaller than the move about a month ago, when the yen briefly fell to around ¥164 per US$1, a near‑40‑year low, before Tokyo and Washington jointly stepped in to support it, pushing the yen up roughly 5%.

That episode marked the first coordinated yen‑buying by the United States and Japan since 1998 and was a rare joint intervention in decades. Both governments later hinted that, if necessary, they would not rule out another coordinated action, dramatically raising the risk of shorting the yen. With the ¥160 barrier breached again, traders are watching closely to see whether officials have already acted quietly or are preparing a new round of intervention.

items.title: 貝森特把日銀逼入死局！升息1碼怕市場不買單 不升日元恐再崩
items.title_en: Bessent Forces BOJ into a Deadlock! Raising Rates by One Point Risks Market Rejection; Not Raising Yen May Cause Further Collapse
paras: 日本銀行(BOJ)將於9月17日至18日召開政策會議，總裁植田和男正陷入罕見的進退兩難局面。美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)近期公開敦促日本升息，市場也已完全反映本月升息1碼的預期；然而，日銀無論升息或按兵不動，都可能引發金融市場劇烈波動。
日銀目前政策利率為1%。期貨與交換市場顯示，投資人已完全反映本月升息1碼至1.25%的可能性。若日銀按兵不動，不僅將讓市場大感意外，也可能導致日元重挫，進一步推升進口成本與通膨。市場預估，日本通膨率今年稍後可能接近3%。
然而，僅升息1碼(25個基點)也未必足以穩定市場。日銀審議委員高田創周三(2日)提出可能採取更大幅度行動的構想，並暗示不排除連續升息，使一般幅度的升息可能更難滿足投資人期待。
摩根大通證券首席日本經濟學家Ayako Fujita表示，美方已將話說到這種程度，日銀若不採取行動恐怕會引發問題；但如果市場認為日銀只能在美國支持下升息，也可能損害政策效果及央行公信力。

日元與日債市場同陷不安

日本債市近期持續遭到拋售，10年期公債殖利率周二突破3%，為1996年以來首見；同期間，美國10年期公債殖利率逼近4.82%，升至貝森特上任前以來最高水準。
貝森特自去年起便多次敦促日銀收緊貨幣政策，主要擔心日本公債市場動盪外溢至美國。日元貶值也可能迫使日本出售持有的美債以進行匯市干預，進而加重美債賣壓並推升美國借貸成本。
樂天證券經濟研究所首席經濟學家、前日銀官員Nobuyasu Atago指出，貝森特之所以敦促日銀升息，是因為他相信此舉有助抑制全球公債殖利率上升，最終也將使美國受惠。
貝森特近日透過社群貼文、媒體訪問及會談持續向日本施壓，要求日銀「做正確的事」，並敦促東京結束再通膨政策。他本周在美國北卡羅來納州舉行的G20會議期間與植田和男會面，雙方討論如何透過健全的政策制定穩定通膨預期，並避免匯率過度波動。

不升息恐讓匯市干預成果付諸流水

植田和男至今未釋出日銀可能將行動延後至10月的訊號。他在G20會議後表示，政策委員會將把物價上行風險納入決策考量，被市場解讀為暗示9月可能升息。高田創隨後更提出連續升息的可能性；日銀最近一次升息是在6月，與前一次行動相隔6個月。
若日銀在市場已完全押注升息的情況下按兵不動，日元可能再度重挫，也可能招致貝森特強烈反應。美日7月31日罕見聯手買進日元，為1998年以來首次共同干預匯市，一度使日元從1986年來低點、約164日元兌1美元，回升至接近155日元。日元周三在紐約市場約報158.72日元，交易員仍警戒美日再次出手干預。
Marlborough Investment Management基金經理James Athey表示，日銀必須升息並發出更強硬訊號，否則先前支撐日元的努力可能付諸流水。他認為，日銀7月未在匯市干預與政治表態已經鋪路的情況下升息，是一項重大錯誤。
不過，分析師認為，日本長期殖利率上升的核心原因並非日銀政策，而是市場對政府財政赤字的疑慮。若日本政府無法提出可信的財政方針，即使日銀升息，也未必能同時阻止日元走弱與長期公債殖利率攀升。
paras_en: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will hold its policy meeting on September 17‑18, putting President Kazuo Ueda in a rare dilemma. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has recently urged Japan to raise rates, and markets have fully priced in a one‑point hike this month; however, whether the BOJ hikes or stays put could trigger sharp market turbulence.

The BOJ’s policy rate stands at 1%. Futures and swap markets show investors have fully priced in a one‑point rise to 1.25% this month. If the BOJ stays idle, it will not only surprise the market but could also cause the yen to slump, further raising import costs and inflation. Markets estimate Japan’s inflation rate may approach 3% later this year.

Yet, a single one‑point (25 basis points) hike may not stabilize the market. BOJ policy committee member Takada Sō announced on Wednesday (2) that a larger move might be considered, hinting that consecutive hikes are not ruled out, making a modest increase harder to satisfy investors’ expectations.

Morgan Stanley Securities chief Japanese economist Ayako Fujita said the U.S. has pushed the issue to this extent; if the BOJ does nothing, problems may arise. However, if the market believes the BOJ can only hike with U.S. support, it could damage policy effectiveness and central bank credibility.

The yen and Japanese bond market are both uneasy. Japan’s bond market has been under selling pressure, with the 10‑year yield breaking 3% on Tuesday for the first time since 1996; meanwhile, the U.S. 10‑year yield approached 4.82%, rising to its highest level since Bessent took office.

Since last year, Bessent has repeatedly urged the BOJ to tighten policy, mainly worried that volatility in Japan’s bond market could spill over to the U.S. A weaker yen could force Japan to sell its U.S. bonds to intervene in the FX market, further increasing selling pressure on U.S. bonds and raising U.S. borrowing costs.
Lotte Securities’ chief economist and former BOJ official Nobuyasu Atago said Bessent’s push for a hike stems from his belief that it will curb global bond yields, ultimately benefiting the U.S.

Bessent has recently used social media posts, media interviews, and talks to pressure Japan, urging the BOJ to "do the right thing" and push Tokyo to end its inflation policy. This week, during the G20 meeting in North Carolina, he met Ueda and discussed how sound policy could stabilize inflation expectations and avoid excessive currency volatility.

Ueda has not yet signaled that the BOJ might delay action until October. After the G20 meeting, he said the policy committee would incorporate price‑upward risk into decisions, which the market interpreted as a hint of a September hike. Takada Sō then suggested the possibility of consecutive hikes; the BOJ’s last hike was in June, six months after the previous one.

If the BOJ remains idle while markets have fully bet on a hike, the yen could slump again and provoke a strong reaction from Bessent. On July 31, the U.S. and Japan jointly bought yen—a rare move since 1998—temporarily lifting the yen from its low of about 164 per dollar to nearly 155. On Wednesday, the yen traded around 158.72 in New York, with traders wary of another intervention.

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough Investment Management, said the BOJ must hike and send a stronger signal, otherwise previous efforts to support the yen could be wasted. He believes the BOJ’s July decision not to intervene in the FX market and make a political statement was a major mistake.

However, analysts say the core reason for rising long‑term yields in Japan is not BOJ policy but market concerns over government fiscal deficits. If the Japanese government cannot present a credible fiscal plan, even a BOJ hike may not simultaneously stop the yen from weakening and long‑term bond yields from climbing.

items.title: 全球債券大幅回檔！但與2022年慘烈災情相比仍是小巫見大巫
items.title_en: Global Bonds Plunge Sharply, Yet Still a Mere Trifle Compared to the 2022 Disaster
paras: 全球債券市場近期遭遇的拋售看來相當慘烈，但與四年前相比仍是小巫見大巫。
回顧2022年時，以聯準會(Fed)為首的各國央行展開半世紀以來最同步且迅速的貨幣政策緊縮行動，以對抗疫情後需求反彈所引發、又受到俄烏戰爭進一步推升的通膨，最終導致全球債券陷入一個世代以來首見的熊市。
如今這波拋售雖然把全球主要市場的債券殖利率推升至多年高點，但漲幅僅是2022年底那波行情的一小部分。
債券殖利率與價格走勢相反。彭博彙整的數據顯示，全球政府債券殖利率過去20日累計上升17個基點，遠低於當時20天內急升的62個基點。
以今年以來的高點至低點計算，債券價格下跌4.2%，與2022年高達23%的跌幅相去甚遠。
儘管目前債市拋售絲毫沒有停歇跡象，但殖利率迄今漲幅相對溫和，讓資深市場觀察人士稍感安心。
自1983年起便追蹤債券市場的投資管理公司GSFM駐雪梨顧問Stephen Miller說，「也許該吃顆定心丸，冷靜一下。我不能說債券現在是強力買進標的」，但以目前這類殖利率水準來看，對以收益為導向的投資人而言，「確實開始值得考慮」。
和2022年造成債市崩跌的原因相比，通膨這一次同樣是重要因素，尤其是伊朗戰爭推升能源價格的影響，但還有其他力量正在加重債券市場壓力。
日本、英國和美國等主要市場政府支出龐大，持續推高發債量，促使投資人要求更高報酬，才能持有較長天期的政府債券。與此同時，人工智慧(AI)熱潮需要龐大資金投入，也加劇資本競爭，進一步推高借貸成本。
即便如此，債券跌幅仍相對獲得控制，部分原因在於目前殖利率是從較高水準上升，因此能提供投資人更大的利息收入緩衝，以抵銷債券價格下跌的影響。相較之下，2022年初殖利率仍接近歷史低點。
今年彭博全球國債總報酬指數成分債券的平均票面利率為2.68%，從2022年的1.84%上升。
摩根大通資產管理公司(JPMorgan Asset Management)駐墨爾本全球市場策略師Kerry Craig說：「對每個經濟體而言，情況並沒有債市表現看起來那麼糟。」他指出，在澳洲等部分市場，投資人甚至可能高估央行升息幅度。
近期經濟數據也支持這項看法。美國部分關鍵經濟數據令人失望，7月非農就業人數下滑，零售銷售也意外下降。日本第2經濟季成長同樣低於預期。
儘管如此，目前還沒人敢斷言殖利率已經觸頂。在能源價格推升通膨的情況下，市場持續押注升息，加上大量政府發債把殖利率進一步推高，債券價格可能還有進一步下跌空間。
日本殖利率上升也是另一項潛在壓力來源，因為日本債券殖利率走高可能吸引全球資金回流日本。
作為全球借貸成本重要基準的10年期美債殖利率，在周三(2日)升至4.81%，創2023年底以來最高，進一步加重其他已開發市場債券的壓力。日本10年期公債殖利率周二觸及3%，為本世紀首次突破這一關卡。
不過從市場波動率降低這一點可以看出，投資人對這一波債市拋售的承受度正在提高：全球政府債券殖利率波動率，已從5月的56個基點高峰下降至37個基點。而在2022年，該指標曾大幅飆升，並在隔年3月攀抵約92個基點。
三井住友信託銀行(Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank)駐東京資深市場策略師Ayako Sera說：「債券市場的負面因素正在逐步累積，但截至目前為止，還沒有出現足以迫使投資人撤出市場的決定性催化劑。」

paras_en: The recent sell‑off in the global bond market looks severe, but it is a mere trifle compared with four years ago.

Looking back to 2022, central banks led by the Federal Reserve launched the most synchronized and rapid monetary tightening in half a century to combat post‑pandemic demand rebound‑driven inflation that was further amplified by the Russia‑Ukraine war, ultimately plunging global bonds into a generational bear market.
Now this wave of selling has pushed yields in major markets to multi‑year highs, yet the rise is only a fraction of the surge seen at the end of 2022.

Bond yields move opposite to prices. Bloomberg‑compiled data show that global government bond yields have risen 17 basis points over the past 20 days, far below the 62‑basis‑point jump in the same span back then.
From this year’s peak to trough, bond prices have fallen 4.2%, a far cry from the 23% plunge recorded in 2022.
Although the bond‑market sell‑off shows no sign of abating, the modest rise in yields so far gives seasoned market observers a bit of comfort.

Stephen Miller, a Sydney‑based adviser at GSFM, which has tracked the bond market since 1983, said, “Maybe take a calming pill and step back. I can’t say bonds are a strong buy right now,” but at current yield levels, “they do start to look worth considering for yield‑focused investors.”

Compared with the drivers of the 2022 bond‑market collapse, inflation remains a key factor this time, especially the impact of the Iran war on energy prices, but other forces are also adding pressure to the market.

Large fiscal outlays in major economies such as Japan, the UK and the US keep issuance high, forcing investors to demand higher returns to hold longer‑dated sovereigns. At the same time, the AI boom requires massive capital, intensifying competition for funds and pushing borrowing costs higher.

Nevertheless, bond declines remain relatively contained, partly because yields are rising from already elevated levels, providing investors with larger interest‑income buffers to offset price drops. By contrast, yields at the start of 2022 were still near historic lows.
The average coupon of the bonds that make up Bloomberg’s Global Government Bond Total Return Index this year is 2.68%, up from 1.84% in 2022.

Kerry Craig, a global market strategist in Melbourne for JPMorgan Asset Management, said, “The situation isn’t as bleak as bond performance alone suggests for any economy.” He noted that in markets such as Australia, investors may even be over‑estimating central‑bank rate hikes.

Recent economic data support that view. Key U.S. indicators disappointed, with July non‑farm payrolls falling and retail sales unexpectedly dropping. Japan’s second‑quarter growth also came in below expectations.

Nonetheless, no one can yet claim yields have peaked. With energy‑price‑driven inflation, markets continue betting on further rate hikes, and massive sovereign issuance pushes yields higher, leaving room for bond prices to fall further.
Rising Japanese yields add another potential pressure source, as higher Japan bond yields could attract global capital back to Japan.

The benchmark 10‑year U.S. Treasury yield, a key global borrowing cost indicator, rose to 4.81% on Wednesday (the 2nd), its highest since the end of 2023, further stressing other developed‑market bonds. Japan’s 10‑year gilt hit 3% on Tuesday, a first‑century breakthrough.

However, lower volatility shows investors are becoming more tolerant of this bond‑sell‑off: global government bond yield volatility has fallen from a May peak of 56 basis points to 37 basis points. In 2022 the metric surged and reached about 92 basis points in March of the following year.

Ayako Sera, a senior market strategist in Tokyo for Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank, said, “Negative factors in the bond market are accumulating gradually, but so far there’s no decisive catalyst that would force investors out of the market.”

items.title: 美日又出手了？日元跌破160後突然暴力拉升 市場瘋傳干預猜測
items.title_en: US and Japan Act Again? Yen Falls Below 160 Then Suddenly Surges, Sparking Intervention Rumors
paras: 日元周三(2日)盤中突然快速升值，在20國集團(G20)會議即將落幕之際，引發日本與美國可能再次進場干預匯市的揣測。由於當時沒有明顯新聞或總體經濟因素足以解釋這波走勢，市場交易室隨即傳出官方出手買進日元的說法。
日元稍早一度貶破160日元兌1美元，隨後突然急速反彈，但漲勢並未持續擴大。市場人士認為，160日元可能已成為美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)與日本銀行(BOJ)共同防守的新底線。
美國銀行(BAC-US)外匯策略師Alex Cohen表示，市場仍對匯市干預保持高度警戒。部分交易員則認為，這波升勢可能只是市場掃除停損單，也就是日元貶破關鍵價位後，引發大量部位自動平倉；不過，仍不能排除相關走勢是由官方力量觸發。
Monex外匯交易員Andrew Hazlett表示，市場確實傳出官方干預的消息，但就本次波動幅度而言，他對這項說法持懷疑態度。然而，日元兌美元與歐元同時突然走強，也很難以其他原因解釋。
這次日元升幅仍小於約一個月前的行情。當時日元一度貶至約164日元兌1美元，創近40年低點，隨後東京與華府聯手進場支撐日元，推動日元反彈約5%。
那是美日自1998年以來首次協調買進日元，也是數十年來罕見的聯合匯市干預。兩國政府事後均暗示，如有必要不排除再次採取共同行動，大幅提高做空日元的風險。隨著160日元關卡再度失守，交易員正密切觀察官方是否已悄然出手，或準備進行新一輪干預。
paras_en: The yen suddenly surged mid‑session on Wednesday (the 2nd), just as the G20 summit was winding down, prompting speculation that Japan and the United States might intervene in the currency market again. Because there was no obvious news or macro‑economic factor to explain the move, market desks quickly began circulating rumors that officials were buying yen.

Earlier the yen had slipped past the ¥160 per US$1 mark, then abruptly rebounded, though the rally did not continue to expand. Market participants think the ¥160 level may have become a new defensive floor jointly defended by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and the Bank of Japan.

Bank of America (BAC-US) FX strategist Alex Cohen said the market remains on high alert for currency‑market intervention. Some traders believe the rise may simply be a market‑wide stop‑loss sweep—positions automatically liquidated after the yen broke a key level—but they do not rule out that the move was triggered by official forces.

Monex FX trader Andrew Hazlett noted that rumors of official intervention are indeed circulating, but given the modest size of this move he is skeptical of that claim. Still, the simultaneous strength of the yen against both the dollar and the euro is hard to explain by any other reason.

The current yen gain is smaller than the move about a month ago, when the yen briefly fell to around ¥164 per US$1, a near‑40‑year low, before Tokyo and Washington jointly stepped in to support it, pushing the yen up roughly 5%.

That episode marked the first coordinated yen‑buying by the United States and Japan since 1998 and was a rare joint intervention in decades. Both governments later hinted that, if necessary, they would not rule out another coordinated action, dramatically raising the risk of shorting the yen. With the ¥160 barrier breached again, traders are watching closely to see whether officials have already acted quietly or are preparing a new round of intervention.

items.title: 貝森特把日銀逼入死局！升息1碼怕市場不買單 不升日元恐再崩
items.title_en: Bessent Forces BOJ into a Deadlock! Raising Rates by One Point Risks Market Rejection; Not Raising Yen May Cause Further Collapse
paras: 日本銀行(BOJ)將於9月17日至18日召開政策會議，總裁植田和男正陷入罕見的進退兩難局面。美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)近期公開敦促日本升息，市場也已完全反映本月升息1碼的預期；然而，日銀無論升息或按兵不動，都可能引發金融市場劇烈波動。
日銀目前政策利率為1%。期貨與交換市場顯示，投資人已完全反映本月升息1碼至1.25%的可能性。若日銀按兵不動，不僅將讓市場大感意外，也可能導致日元重挫，進一步推升進口成本與通膨。市場預估，日本通膨率今年稍後可能接近3%。
然而，僅升息1碼(25個基點)也未必足以穩定市場。日銀審議委員高田創周三(2日)提出可能採取更大幅度行動的構想，並暗示不排除連續升息，使一般幅度的升息可能更難滿足投資人期待。
摩根大通證券首席日本經濟學家Ayako Fujita表示，美方已將話說到這種程度，日銀若不採取行動恐怕會引發問題；但如果市場認為日銀只能在美國支持下升息，也可能損害政策效果及央行公信力。

日元與日債市場同陷不安

日本債市近期持續遭到拋售，10年期公債殖利率周二突破3%，為1996年以來首見；同期間，美國10年期公債殖利率逼近4.82%，升至貝森特上任前以來最高水準。
貝森特自去年起便多次敦促日銀收緊貨幣政策，主要擔心日本公債市場動盪外溢至美國。日元貶值也可能迫使日本出售持有的美債以進行匯市干預，進而加重美債賣壓並推升美國借貸成本。
樂天證券經濟研究所首席經濟學家、前日銀官員Nobuyasu Atago指出，貝森特之所以敦促日銀升息，是因為他相信此舉有助抑制全球公債殖利率上升，最終也將使美國受惠。
貝森特近日透過社群貼文、媒體訪問及會談持續向日本施壓，要求日銀「做正確的事」，並敦促東京結束再通膨政策。他本周在美國北卡羅來納州舉行的G20會議期間與植田和男會面，雙方討論如何透過健全的政策制定穩定通膨預期，並避免匯率過度波動。

不升息恐讓匯市干預成果付諸流水

植田和男至今未釋出日銀可能將行動延後至10月的訊號。他在G20會議後表示，政策委員會將把物價上行風險納入決策考量，被市場解讀為暗示9月可能升息。高田創隨後更提出連續升息的可能性；日銀最近一次升息是在6月，與前一次行動相隔6個月。
若日銀在市場已完全押注升息的情況下按兵不動，日元可能再度重挫，也可能招致貝森特強烈反應。美日7月31日罕見聯手買進日元，為1998年以來首次共同干預匯市，一度使日元從1986年來低點、約164日元兌1美元，回升至接近155日元。日元周三在紐約市場約報158.72日元，交易員仍警戒美日再次出手干預。
Marlborough Investment Management基金經理James Athey表示，日銀必須升息並發出更強硬訊號，否則先前支撐日元的努力可能付諸流水。他認為，日銀7月未在匯市干預與政治表態已經鋪路的情況下升息，是一項重大錯誤。
不過，分析師認為，日本長期殖利率上升的核心原因並非日銀政策，而是市場對政府財政赤字的疑慮。若日本政府無法提出可信的財政方針，即使日銀升息，也未必能同時阻止日元走弱與長期公債殖利率攀升。
paras_en: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will hold its policy meeting on September 17‑18, putting President Kazuo Ueda in a rare dilemma. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has recently urged Japan to raise rates, and markets have fully priced in a one‑point hike this month; however, whether the BOJ hikes or stays put could trigger sharp market turbulence.

The BOJ’s policy rate stands at 1%. Futures and swap markets show investors have fully priced in a one‑point rise to 1.25% this month. If the BOJ stays idle, it will not only surprise the market but could also cause the yen to slump, further raising import costs and inflation. Markets estimate Japan’s inflation rate may approach 3% later this year.

Yet, a single one‑point (25 basis points) hike may not stabilize the market. BOJ policy committee member Takada Sō announced on Wednesday (2) that a larger move might be considered, hinting that consecutive hikes are not ruled out, making a modest increase harder to satisfy investors’ expectations.

Morgan Stanley Securities chief Japanese economist Ayako Fujita said the U.S. has pushed the issue to this extent; if the BOJ does nothing, problems may arise. However, if the market believes the BOJ can only hike with U.S. support, it could damage policy effectiveness and central bank credibility.

The yen and Japanese bond market are both uneasy. Japan’s bond market has been under selling pressure, with the 10‑year yield breaking 3% on Tuesday for the first time since 1996; meanwhile, the U.S. 10‑year yield approached 4.82%, rising to its highest level since Bessent took office.

Since last year, Bessent has repeatedly urged the BOJ to tighten policy, mainly worried that volatility in Japan’s bond market could spill over to the U.S. A weaker yen could force Japan to sell its U.S. bonds to intervene in the FX market, further increasing selling pressure on U.S. bonds and raising U.S. borrowing costs.
Lotte Securities’ chief economist and former BOJ official Nobuyasu Atago said Bessent’s push for a hike stems from his belief that it will curb global bond yields, ultimately benefiting the U.S.

Bessent has recently used social media posts, media interviews, and talks to pressure Japan, urging the BOJ to "do the right thing" and push Tokyo to end its inflation policy. This week, during the G20 meeting in North Carolina, he met Ueda and discussed how sound policy could stabilize inflation expectations and avoid excessive currency volatility.

Ueda has not yet signaled that the BOJ might delay action until October. After the G20 meeting, he said the policy committee would incorporate price‑upward risk into decisions, which the market interpreted as a hint of a September hike. Takada Sō then suggested the possibility of consecutive hikes; the BOJ’s last hike was in June, six months after the previous one.

If the BOJ remains idle while markets have fully bet on a hike, the yen could slump again and provoke a strong reaction from Bessent. On July 31, the U.S. and Japan jointly bought yen—a rare move since 1998—temporarily lifting the yen from its low of about 164 per dollar to nearly 155. On Wednesday, the yen traded around 158.72 in New York, with traders wary of another intervention.

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough Investment Management, said the BOJ must hike and send a stronger signal, otherwise previous efforts to support the yen could be wasted. He believes the BOJ’s July decision not to intervene in the FX market and make a political statement was a major mistake.

However, analysts say the core reason for rising long‑term yields in Japan is not BOJ policy but market concerns over government fiscal deficits. If the Japanese government cannot present a credible fiscal plan, even a BOJ hike may not simultaneously stop the yen from weakening and long‑term bond yields from climbing.

items.title: 〈台幣〉熱錢撤出股匯雙殺 放量貶近1角收31.728元
items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Loses Hot Money as Stocks and Currency Fall Together, Declining Nearly 0.1 TWD to Close at 31.728 per USD
paras: 美國與伊朗軍事衝突再次升溫，推升國際油價走揚，市場避險情緒順勢帶動美元走強。台北股匯今(2)日連袂走弱，在外資熱錢加速撤出下，新台幣兌美元一度摜破 31.8 元關卡，終場貶勢收斂，收在 31.728 元、貶值 9.5 分，為逾 1 周新低。台北及元太外匯市場總成交值放大至 37.48 億美元。
新台幣兌美元今天以31.65元開盤後，隨著美元買盤湧現，匯價接連失守31.7元、31.8元兩道關卡，最低下探 31.804 元、重貶 1.71 角，不過，在央行尾盤調節下，貶幅快速收斂，終場以 31.728 元作收。
台股今天震盪走跌，加權指數終場收在46164.72點，下跌784點，跌幅1.67%，台積電賣壓沉重，終場下跌 55 元。三大法人同步站在賣方，合計賣超台股1150.33億元，其中外資大舉提款913.54億元。
主要亞幣今日普遍走弱，根據央行統計，美元指數上漲 0.11%，新台幣貶值 0.3% 最弱，新加坡幣貶0.04%，人民幣貶0.01%，而韓元強升 0.53%，日元也升值 0.18%，亞幣走勢不同調。
近期地緣政治局勢顯著升溫，美軍對伊朗伊斯蘭革命衛隊發動打擊以回應其海峽布雷與基地位址襲擊，導致中東緊張局勢加劇。此事件直接引發全球能源供應擔憂，驅使國際油價大幅飆升，布蘭特原油突破每桶 95 美元、西德州原油重回 90 美元大關，進一步加劇了市場對全球通膨重燃的疑慮。
油價大漲與通膨預期抬頭，加上聯準會官員釋出鷹派訊號及市場對美財政赤字的擔憂，引發全球債市遭遇拋售，美國 10 年期公債殖利率大幅飆升。在此背景下，避險資金積極湧入美元，加上高油價對美國貿易條件的相對優勢與升息預期的支撐，推升美元指數強勢走高，歐元與日元等主要貨幣則相對承壓。
paras_en: U.S. and Iranian military tensions escalated again, pushing up international oil prices and strengthening the dollar as investors sought safety. Taipei’s stock and currency markets both weakened today (the 2nd), and as foreign hot money rushed out, the New Taiwan dollar briefly broke the 31.8 per‑dollar barrier before the decline eased, closing at 31.728, a depreciation of 9.5 cents and a new low for more than a week. The total turnover in Taipei and Yuan‑Tai foreign‑exchange markets expanded to US$3.748 billion.

The New Taiwan dollar opened at 31.65 per USD, but as dollar buying surged the rate slipped through the 31.7 and 31.8 thresholds, sinking to a low of 31.804 – a drop of 0.171 TWD. However, the central bank’s end‑of‑day intervention quickly narrowed the loss, and the session ended at 31.728.

Taiwan’s stock market wavered lower, with the weighted index finishing at 46,164.72 points, down 784 points or 1.67%. TSMC faced heavy selling, dropping 55 TWD by close. The three major institutional investors all acted as sellers, netting a total sell‑off of NT$115.033 billion, of which foreign investors withdrew a massive NT$91.354 billion.

Major Asian currencies were broadly weaker today. According to central‑bank data, the U.S. dollar index rose 0.11%, the New Taiwan dollar weakened the most at –0.3%, the Singapore dollar fell 0.04%, the Chinese yuan slipped 0.01%, while the Korean won rose 0.53% and the Japanese yen gained 0.18%, showing divergent moves among Asian currencies.

Geopolitical tensions have risen sharply. The U.S. military struck Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in response to attacks on a strait and a base, heightening Middle‑East tensions. The incident sparked global concerns over energy supply, sending international oil prices soaring – Brent crude broke US$95 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate reclaimed the US$90 level, further stoking worries about a resurgence of global inflation.

Rising oil prices and inflation expectations, combined with hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials and worries about the U.S. fiscal deficit, triggered a sell‑off in global bond markets, sending U.S. 10‑year Treasury yields sharply higher. In this backdrop, safe‑haven flows poured into the dollar, and high oil prices boosted the U.S. trade‑condition advantage and rate‑hike expectations, pushing the dollar index higher while the euro, yen and other major currencies faced relative pressure.

items.title: 日銀審議委員高田創釋鷹派訊號 暗示加速升息步伐
items.title_en: Bank of Japan Board Member Takada Signals Hawkish Tone, Hinting at Accelerated Rate Hikes
paras: 日本央行審議委員高田創周三(2日)在札幌召開的記者會上，釋出強烈鷹派訊號。他表示，未來的升息幅度不排除超過常規的0.25%，且連續升息也是可能的選項，顯示日銀可能加速貨幣緊縮步伐。
日銀過去三次升息均以0.25%的幅度進行，且間隔約6個月，但高田創強調這並非一成不變。他指出，隨著日本經濟在2026年步入「機制轉變」的新階段，2%的物價穩定目標已基本實現，升息步伐將靈活且依賴數據，以因應國內外的價格與經濟風險。
在先前的7月會議中，高田曾投下唯一的反對票，倡議直接升息25個基點至1.25%。
高田創的發言讓市場對日銀在9月18日政策會議上升息的預期顯著升溫，日元匯率隨之走強，一度回升至1美元兌159.80日元附近。日銀總裁植田和男此前暗示，將在考慮上行價格風險的前提下做出決策，增添了本月升息的可能性。
與此同時，受到首相高市早苗擴張性財政政策預期及日銀減少購債影響，日本10年期公債殖利率30年來首度突破3%。高田對此強調，日銀減少購債旨在維護市場穩定並避免過度波動，而非迎合國家的財政狀況。
摩根大通分析師指出，高田的言論反映了日銀內部的整體鷹派轉變，預計日銀將於9月與12月分別升息25個基點。
paras_en: On Wednesday (2nd), Bank of Japan board member Takada Saku gave a strongly hawkish signal at a press conference in Sapporo, stating that future rate hikes could exceed the conventional 0.25% and that consecutive hikes are also a possibility, indicating that the BOJ may accelerate its monetary tightening pace.

The BOJ has previously raised rates three times by 0.25% each, roughly every six months, but Takada emphasized that this is not set in stone. He noted that as Japan’s economy enters a new “mechanism shift” phase in 2026, the 2% inflation target is essentially achieved, and the pace of hikes will be flexible and data‑dependent to respond to domestic and global price and economic risks.
During the July meeting, Takada cast the sole dissenting vote, advocating a direct 25‑basis‑point hike to 1.25%.

Takada’s remarks stoked market expectations of a rate hike at the September 18 policy meeting, strengthening the yen as it briefly rebounded to around 159.80 yen per dollar. BOJ Governor Ueda had previously hinted that a decision would be made considering upward price risks, adding to the likelihood of a hike this month.

Meanwhile, amid expectations of Prime Minister Fumio Kishida’s expansionary fiscal policy and the BOJ’s reduced bond purchases, the yield on Japan’s 10‑year government bonds broke 3% for the first time in 30 years. Takada stressed that the BOJ’s bond‑purchase cuts aim to maintain market stability and avoid excessive volatility, not to accommodate the country’s fiscal situation.
Morgan Stanley analysts noted that Takada’s comments reflect a broader hawkish shift within the BOJ, forecasting 25‑basis‑point hikes in both September and December.

items.title: 紐西蘭央行再度升息1碼至2.75% 釋放鴿派緊縮訊號 紐元走跌
items.title_en: New Zealand Central Bank Raises Rates Again by 0.25% to 2.75%, Signalling Dovish Tightening; NZD Slides
paras: 紐西蘭央行周三(2日)宣布將基準利率上調25個基點(1碼)至2.75%。這是央行繼7月後連續第二次升息，旨在抑制高企的通膨。然而，央行透露未來緊縮路徑將比預期更為溫和，導致紐西蘭元應聲重挫達1%，兩年期公債殖利率下跌7個基點至3.58%。
交換合約數據顯示，市場預期10月升息的機率由之前的65%驟降至約36%。
紐西蘭第二季消費者物價指數(CPI)年增率達4.1%，主因是中東衝突推升燃料價格。不過，剔除車用燃料的核心通膨率已回落至2.7%至2.9%之間。央行預估，通膨將在2028年初回到2%的目標中位數。
針對未來利率政策，央行總裁 Anna Breman 指出，「基準利率很可能需要進一步調升」，但升息時機仍具高度不確定性，決策官員需綜合評估前兩次升息累積的效應與後續的經濟數據。
對此，Westpac 銀行紐西蘭首席經濟學家 Kelly Eckhold 分析，央行雖有升息決心，但目前看來，這比較像是12月而非10月和12月都會討論的議題。研調機構 Capital Economics 則認為，央行的訊息「比先前少了一些鷹派色彩」，並預測基準利率將在2027年上半年達到3.25%的峰值，低於市場預期的3.75%。
Kiwibank 首席經濟學家 Jarrod Kerr 表達了對此決策的讚許，並預期年底前僅會再升息一次至3.0%，隨後進入長期停頓。相對地，ASB 資深經濟學家 Mark Smith 則維持原有預估，認為10月及12月將各升息1碼，使年底基準利率達到3.25%的中性水準。
paras_en: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand announced on Wednesday (the 2nd) that it is raising the official cash rate by 25 basis points (one tick) to 2.75%. This is the second consecutive hike since July, aimed at curbing elevated inflation. However, the bank signaled that the future tightening path will be milder than expected, sending the New Zealand dollar down about 1% and pushing the two‑year government bond yield down 7 basis points to 3.58%.
Futures data show that the market’s probability of a rate hike in October fell sharply from about 65% to roughly 36%.

New Zealand’s consumer price index (CPI) for the second quarter rose 4.1% year‑on‑year, driven mainly by higher fuel prices due to the Middle East conflict. Core inflation, which excludes motor fuel, has eased to a range of 2.7%‑2.9%. The central bank projects that inflation will return to the 2% target midpoint in early 2028.

Regarding future policy, RBNZ Governor Anna Breman said the official cash rate is likely to need further increases, but the timing remains highly uncertain, with policymakers having to weigh the cumulative impact of the first two hikes against upcoming economic data.

Westpac New Zealand chief economist Kelly Eckhold noted that while the bank is determined to tighten, the next move looks more like a December issue rather than October, and Capital Economics argued the message is “somewhat less hawkish than before,” forecasting the cash rate to peak at 3.25% in the first half of 2027, below the market‑based expectation of 3.75%.

Kiwibank chief economist Jarrod Kerr praised the decision and expects only one more hike to 3.0% before year‑end, after which rates would stay on hold for a long period. In contrast, ASB senior economist Mark Smith sticks to his original view that both October and December will see 0.25‑point hikes, taking the year‑end cash rate to a neutral 3.25%.

items.title: 植田和男釋放9月升息強烈訊號！日銀升息預期近100%、日債殖利率飆近30年高
items.title_en: Ueda Kazuo Sends Strong September Rate‑Hike Signal! BoJ Rate‑Hike Expectation Near 100% and JGB Yields Surge to Near‑30‑Year High
paras: 日本銀行總裁植田和男釋出強烈升息訊號，市場對日銀9月再度調升政策利率的預期進一步升溫。植田日前出席美國北卡羅來納州阿什維爾舉行的G20財長與央行總裁會議後表示，日本目前貨幣環境仍相對寬鬆，因此日銀希望持續升息，並將在評估物價上行風險後討論貨幣政策。
植田指出，日銀迄今已累計5度調升政策利率，因此有必要審慎評估累積升息對經濟帶來的影響。下一次政策會議將進一步討論經濟情勢實現的可能性是否提高，以及通膨風險是否加劇。
這也是植田在9月17日至18日日銀政策會議前最後一次公開露面。根據《彭博》報導，隔夜指數交換（OIS）市場顯示，交易員對日銀9月升息的定價已接近100%，而植田此次談話也沒有反駁市場的升息預期。
與此同時，美國聯準會（Fed）鷹派官員也接連釋出強硬訊號。在華許（Kevin Warsh）警告通膨風險後，聯準會理事巴爾（Michael Barr）也表示，如果通膨未能充分降溫，聯準會就應果斷升息。

日銀升息預期升溫　日債殖利率創近30年新高

市場迅速反映日本貨幣政策可能進一步轉向緊縮的預期。10年期日本國債殖利率一度升至3.004%，30年期殖利率則觸及4.197%，雙雙創下近30年新高。
股市同樣承受壓力，日經225指數開盤下跌逾2.53%，報64678.49點，單日跌幅超過1700點；韓國KOSPI指數也同步下挫2.19%。
若日銀在9月18日宣布升息，將創下植田任內兩次升息間隔最短紀錄，打破過去約每6個月一次的貨幣政策正常化節奏。
植田表示，目前經濟數據大致符合日銀7月《展望報告》的預測，對於後續貨幣政策操作的基本思路也沒有重大改變。他同時指出，日本通膨趨勢已非常接近日銀設定的2%目標。
根據《彭博》調查，經濟學家預期日本關鍵價格指標可能在明年初回升至3%。
日銀政策委員會中立場最為鷹派的委員Hajime Takata也進一步強化升息預期。他在北海道札幌發表演說時重申7月主張連續升息的立場，並表示日本經濟已進入新階段，部分受到AI需求大增的影響，日本貨幣政策也不再是「異類」，需要靈活因應包括全球局勢在內的各項變化。

貝森特支持日銀升息　日元兌美元回到160上方

美國財政部表示，美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）週日（30日）與植田和男會面時，強調制定及溝通健全貨幣政策的重要性，藉此穩定通膨預期並避免匯率出現過度波動。
貝森特也對日本為處理日元嚴重低估所採取的「果斷市場和貨幣措施」表達強烈支持，並表示預期植田會在貨幣政策上「做正確的事」，同時認為近期日元走勢「控制得相當好」。
不過，日元近期仍維持弱勢。截至東京時間週三（2日）上午，美元兌日元報160.37，日美兩國7月31日聯合干預匯市後，日元先前的升幅已大致回吐。

日本擴張財政遇上日銀緊縮　政策方向形成拉鋸

另一方面，日本政府各部門正提出規模創紀錄的下一會計年度預算申請，顯示首相高市早苗推動財政擴張的意向。
《彭博》報導指出，此次預算申請規模大幅增加，部分與會計方式調整有關。高市早苗希望終止日本長期在年度預算之外另行編列補充預算的做法。
日本財務大臣片山皋月（Satsuki Katayama）在G20會議後表示，與會各方並未對日本財政狀況表達擔憂。植田則認為，日本國債殖利率走高主要是「跟隨全球趨勢」。
在日本政府持續擴大財政支出的同時，日銀則逐步推進貨幣政策正常化。財政擴張與升息路徑之間的政策張力，正成為牽動日本債券、匯率與股市後續走勢的重要變數。
paras_en: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda issued a strong rate‑hike signal, heating up market expectations that the BOJ will raise its policy rate again in September. After attending the G20 finance ministers and central bank governors meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, Ueda said Japan’s monetary environment remains relatively accommodative, so the BOJ wants to keep raising rates and will discuss policy after assessing inflation‑upside risks.

Ueda noted that the BOJ has already raised its policy rate five times in total, so it needs to carefully evaluate the cumulative impact of hikes on the economy. The next policy meeting will further examine whether the likelihood of achieving the desired economic conditions has risen and whether inflation risks have intensified.

This will be Ueda’s last public appearance before the BOJ policy meeting on September 17‑18. Bloomberg reported that the overnight index swap (OIS) market shows traders pricing a September BOJ hike at almost 100%, and Ueda’s remarks did not contradict the market’s rate‑hike expectations.

At the same time, hawkish Fed officials have been issuing tough signals. After Kevin Warsh warned of inflation risks, Fed Governor Michael Barr said the Fed should act decisively on rate hikes if inflation does not cool sufficiently.

BOJ rate‑hike expectations rise as JGB yields hit near‑30‑year highs. The market quickly reflected expectations of a further tightening shift. The 10‑year Japanese government bond yield briefly rose to 3.004% and the 30‑year yield touched 4.197%, both setting near‑30‑year records.
Equities also felt the pressure, with the Nikkei 225 opening down more than 2.53% at 64,678.49 points, a single‑day drop of over 1,700 points; South Korea’s KOSPI fell 2.19% as well.
If the BOJ announces a hike on September 18, it would mark the shortest interval between two hikes under Ueda’s tenure, breaking the roughly six‑month normalisation rhythm previously observed.

Ueda said current economic data broadly match the BOJ’s July Outlook Report forecasts, and there is no major change to the basic approach for future policy actions. He also pointed out that Japan’s inflation trend is now very close to the BOJ’s 2% target.
A Bloomberg survey found economists expect Japan’s core price indicator could rebound to 3% early next year.

The most hawkish member of the BOJ Policy Board, Hajime Takata, further reinforced rate‑hike expectations. Speaking in Sapporo, Hokkaido, he reiterated his July stance for continued hikes and said Japan’s economy has entered a new phase, partly driven by a surge in AI demand, making monetary policy no longer an “outlier” and requiring flexible responses to global developments.

Bessent backs BOJ hikes; yen climbs back above 160 per dollar. The U.S. Treasury said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met with Ueda on Sunday (the 30th) and stressed the importance of formulating and communicating sound monetary policy to stabilise inflation expectations and avoid excessive exchange‑rate volatility.

Bessent also voiced strong support for Japan’s “decisive market and monetary measures” to address the yen’s severe undervaluation, saying he expects Ueda to “do the right thing” on policy and noting that the yen’s recent move has been “well‑controlled.”

Nevertheless, the yen remains weak. As of Wednesday morning Tokyo time (the 2nd), the dollar was at 160.37 yen, and after the joint Japan‑U.S. intervention on July 31, the yen’s earlier gains have largely been erased.

Japan’s fiscal expansion meets BOJ tightening, creating a policy tug‑of‑war. Meanwhile, various Japanese ministries are submitting a record‑size budget request for the next fiscal year, signalling Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s push for fiscal expansion.

Bloomberg reported that the budget request’s massive increase is partly due to changes in accounting methods. Takaichi aims to end Japan’s long‑standing practice of preparing supplemental budgets outside the annual budget.

Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said after the G20 meeting that participants did not express concerns about Japan’s fiscal situation. Ueda believes the rise in JGB yields is mainly “following global trends.”

As the Japanese government continues to expand fiscal spending, the BOJ is gradually normalising monetary policy. The tension between fiscal expansion and the rate‑hike path is becoming a key factor shaping the future direction of Japanese bonds, the yen and equities.

items.title: 美債崩、日元潰！滙豐：當前亞洲金融環境與1997年危機前夕驚人相似
items.title_en: US Bond Collapse, Yen Plunge! HSBC: Current Asian Financial Environment Strikingly Similar to Pre‑1997 Crisis
paras: 滙豐首席經濟學家Frederick Neumann最新示警，當前亞洲金融環境與1997年危機前夕存在「驚人相似」：美債殖利率飆升、日元持續走弱、科技樂觀情緒瀰漫，三者格局幾乎相同。1997年亞洲金融危機曾讓泰銖、韓元崩盤，資本外逃、銀行倒閉潮席捲多國。
Neumann在最新研究報告中指出，目前美債10年期殖利率從2020年8月0.5%低潮攀至本週約4.79%，光是今年就自2月3.9%跳升80個基點，而反觀1993-1997年，同天期美債殖利率從5%衝至8%區域後在7%附近徘迴。
日元匯率方面，1995年4月美元兌日元匯率觸及80，1997年時貶至130，貶幅55%，而本輪自2021年1月103附近貶值57%至今年7月163，經美日罕見聯合干預才拉高至160，套利平倉隱憂未消。
此外，科技敘事亦很相像，當年網路狂熱，如今AI浪潮點燃南韓、日本、新加坡、台灣等出口榮景。
但Neumann強調，2026年與1997年「差異遠大於相似」，當時亞洲多為資本淨進口國、儲蓄不足，美元融資貴，加上日元狂貶直接引爆外債危機，如今亞洲轉成資本輸出方，外部融資擠壓不再致命，真正弱點是「需求脆弱性」，AI伺服器、HBM、先進封裝等硬體出口已經是成長支柱，若美債長端繼續上逼融資成本、或日元劇烈反轉擾亂全球流動性，外需一旦收縮，亞洲製造業景氣將快速失速。
機構普遍認為，系統性金融危機重演機率低，但「高成長高依賴」模式正進入壓力測試期。投資人宜區分區域套利結構與AI實質訂單，提防題材退潮及利率重估的雙殺。
paras_en: HSBC chief economist Frederick Neumann warned that today’s Asian financial environment bears "astonishing similarity" to the eve of the 1997 crisis: US Treasury yields are soaring, the yen keeps weakening, and tech optimism is pervasive, with the three elements forming almost the same pattern. The 1997 Asian financial crisis saw the Thai baht and South Korean won collapse, capital flight and a wave of bank failures sweeping many countries.

Neumann’s latest research notes that the 10‑year US Treasury yield has risen from a low of 0.5% in August 2020 to about 4.79% this week, jumping 80 basis points since February when it was 3.9%. By contrast, from 1993 to 1997 the same‑maturity yield rose from around 5% to the 8% area before hovering near 7%.

Regarding the yen, the USD/JPY rate hit 80 in April 1995, fell to 130 in 1997 – a 55% depreciation – and this cycle has seen it weaken from around 103 in January 2021 by 57% to 163 in July this year, only nudging up to 160 after a rare joint US‑Japan intervention, leaving arbitrage unwind risks still present.
The tech narrative is also similar: the internet frenzy of the 1990s mirrors today’s AI wave, fueling export booms in South Korea, Japan, Singapore, Taiwan and others.

Neumann stresses that the differences between 2026 and 1997 are far greater than the similarities. Back then most Asian economies were net capital importers with insufficient savings, expensive dollar financing and a sharply depreciating yen that sparked an external‑debt crisis. Today Asia is a net capital exporter, so external financing squeezes are less lethal; the real weakness is “demand fragility.” Hardware exports such as AI servers, HBM and advanced packaging have become growth pillars, but if long‑term US yields keep pushing financing costs up or the yen reverses sharply, disrupting global liquidity, a contraction in external demand could cause Asian manufacturing to stall rapidly.

Institutions generally see a low probability of a repeat systemic financial crisis, but the “high‑growth, high‑dependency” model is entering a stress‑test phase. Investors should differentiate regional arbitrage structures from genuine AI orders and guard against a double‑hit from theme fatigue and rate re‑pricing.

items.title: 人民幣升值衝擊！中國車廠上半年出海狂飆 但匯損逾78億吃掉一半利潤 吉利最慘
items.title_en: Renminbi Appreciation Shock! Chinese Automakers' Overseas Sales Soar in H1 but Exchange Losses Over 7.8 Billion RMB Ate Half Their Profit, Geely Hit the Hardest
paras: 今年上半年，中國汽車業交出慘淡成績單。根據Wind數據，289家汽車製造業上市公司歸母淨利565.31億元(人民幣，下同)，年減25.74%，整車製造利潤率跌至1.5%，創近十年新低，但比產業普跌更刺眼的是，出海越多，被匯率反噬越狠。
奇瑞匯兌淨損失20.92億元，吉利由去年同期26.4億元收益轉5.5億元損失，長城扣除鎖匯後仍損失2.66億元，長安淨損約2.3億元。比亞迪未單列匯兌項目，但財務費用淨支出50.96億元，不同於去年同期32.47億元淨收益，一進一出相差83.43 億元，相當於比亞迪當期歸母淨利123.25 億元的三分之二，浙商證券則計算其中約47億元為匯損。
比亞迪上半年營收3448.15億元，年減7.13%、歸母淨利123.25 億元，年減20.54%，看似雙降，但汽車業務毛利率從20.35%逆勢抬到22.33%，汽車收入持平 。推力來自於海外78.94萬輛銷量，年增67.9%、佔集團銷量44%，方程式豹/騰勢/仰望合計22.8 萬輛，年增61%、佔比升至12.8%。
根據東方證券計算，比亞迪海外汽車毛利率28.4%、國內僅17%，海外單車均價約16.3萬元，高於中國國內14.3萬元。
比亞迪上半年境外收入1812.68 億元，年增33.92%，佔總營收52.57%，史上首次超過中國國內，但出口量成長67.9%遠超收入成長33.92%，單車出口均價較一年前下降約1.6萬元，出口巴西19.47萬輛最多、東南亞、拉美等價格敏感市場比重亦上升，Dolphin MINI在巴西起售價約15萬元稀釋了整體平均售價。
根據中汽協數據，今年上半年比亞迪出口79.2 萬輛，次於奇瑞93.9萬輛，但汽車海外收入1294.97 億元是奇瑞989.68億元的 1.31 倍。
paras_en: In the first half of this year, China's auto industry posted a bleak performance. According to Wind data, the 289 listed auto manufacturers reported a net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 56.531 billion, down 25.74% year‑on‑year, with the overall vehicle manufacturing profit margin falling to 1.5%, a near‑decade low. Even more striking than the industry‑wide decline is that the more they exported, the harsher the blow from exchange‑rate movements.

Chery suffered a net foreign‑exchange loss of RMB 2.092 billion, Geely swung from a RMB 2.64 billion gain in the same period last year to a RMB 5.5 billion loss, Great Wall still lost RMB 266 million after hedging, and Changan posted a net loss of about RMB 230 million. BYD did not list a separate FX item, but its net financial expense was RMB 5.096 billion, a reversal from a RMB 3.247 billion net gain a year earlier—a swing of RMB 8.343 billion, equivalent to two‑thirds of BYD’s net profit of RMB 12.325 billion for the period. Zhejiang Securities estimates that roughly RMB 4.7 billion of this amount was due to exchange losses.

BYD’s H1 revenue was RMB 344.815 billion, down 7.13% year‑on‑year, with net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 12.325 billion, down 20.54%. While both figures fell, the automotive segment’s gross margin rose from 20.35% to 22.33% against the trend, and automotive revenue remained flat. The boost came from overseas sales of 789,400 vehicles, up 67.9% year‑on‑year and accounting for 44% of the group’s total sales. The Formula Leopard/Tengshi/Yaowang models together sold 228,000 units, up 61% and representing 12.8% of sales.

According to calculations by Dongfang Securities, BYD’s overseas vehicle gross margin was 28.4%, compared with only 17% domestically. The average price of an overseas BYD vehicle was about RMB 163,000, higher than the RMB 143,000 average price in China.

In the first half, BYD’s overseas revenue reached RMB 181.268 billion, up 33.92% year‑on‑year and accounting for 52.57% of total revenue – the first time overseas sales have exceeded domestic revenue. Export volume grew 67.9%, far outpacing revenue growth of 33.92%. The average export price per vehicle fell by roughly RMB 16,000 compared with a year earlier. Exports to Brazil topped 194,700 units, and the share of price‑sensitive markets such as Southeast Asia and Latin America also rose. The Dolphin MINI, priced at about RMB 150,000 in Brazil, diluted the overall average selling price.

Data from the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers show that BYD exported 792,000 vehicles in the first half of the year, second only to Chery’s 939,000 units, but BYD’s overseas revenue of RMB 129.497 billion was 1.31 times Chery’s RMB 98.968 billion.
